## Game
Game: Cube Cash Tycoon - Watch cubes roll down your conveyor, cash in, and buy droppers and speed upgrades to grow your tiny factory!
Core loop: Each player gets a bright plot with a dropper that spawns a 1-cash cube every 2 seconds onto a conveyor. The conveyor carries cubes to a collector at the end, and the server adds each cube's value to the player's Cash leaderstat and destroys the cube. Two buy pads sit off to the side of the walking area: a second dropper for 25 cash and a faster conveyor for 50 cash. Touching a pad with enough cash buys the upgrade once, so income climbs and the numbers go up.
Acceptance: The map (baseplate and the player's plot with dropper, conveyor, collector and two buy pads) is built from parts at startup and the 'map_built' counter is 1; The player spawns on their plot within a few seconds, and 'plot_assigned' is 1; 'cubes_dropped' increases within the first 2 seconds and keeps increasing roughly every 2 seconds; 'cubes_collected' increases as cubes reach the collector, and the Cash leaderstat rises; Touching a buy pad with insufficient cash does nothing; with enough cash it deducts the cost once and increments 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought'; The HUD shows the current Cash and updates as it changes; Walking from spawn does not trigger the buy pads accidentally, and the cube count stays under the cap; No errors or warnings appear in the output; At startup the plaza (stone tiles, fountain, lamp posts, trees) and 6 plots in a ring exist; 'plaza_built' is 1, 'themes_built' is 6 and 'map_built' is 1; Each plot has a distinct theme floor material and color plus 3-5 decoration props (lollipops, lava cracks, crystals, palm trees, neon strips, cacti), and no part is default grey; rails, dropper bodies and pads use theme colors; Players spawn in the plaza, not on a plot, and cubes_dropped stays 0 until a plot is claimed; Each free plot shows a glowing gate with a BillboardGui reading 'Claim <Theme> Plot'; Walking onto a gate claims that plot: the sign shows the player's name, the gate hides, 'plots_claimed' and 'plot_assigned' increase, and 'cubes_dropped' starts rising about every 2 seconds; A player who does not claim within 20 seconds is auto-claimed to the nearest free plot ('auto_claims' increases) and the dropper starts; ReplicatedStorage/Upgrades has 10 upgrades with unique ids, every requires id exists, and the first purchase (Dropper 2) costs 10; After claiming a plot, only the Dropper 2 pad is visible on that plot, with a billboard showing its name and '$10'; Within about 10 seconds of claiming, Cash reaches 10 and the Dropper 2 pad turns the plot accent color; Touching Dropper 2 with enough cash deducts 10 exactly once, the pad vanishes, the Silver, Speed 1 and Dropper 3 pads appear, and 'upgrades_bought' increments; Touching a pad with insufficient cash, or whose parent is not owned, does nothing and deducts nothing; After Dropper 2 is bought, two cubes spawn per drop cycle and 'cubes_dropped' rises faster

## Feature request
Visible plot growth, split into SMALL modules (each well under 200 lines; the coder's output cap was hit by a single big file last time). The plot is a big empty floor and buying upgrades barely changes how it looks. (1) ServerScriptService/GrowthModels.luau: pure model builders, one short function per kind, each returning a Model built from 3-8 anchored parts in the given theme colors (never default grey): dropperMachine(cf, theme), chevrons(cf, theme), orePile(cf, theme, tierColor), vault(cf, theme, label), plotWall(plotCFrame, size, theme). (2) ServerScriptService/PlotGrowth.luau: the service. PlotGrowth.apply(player, plot, ownedIds) builds the missing models for every owned upgrade (Dropper 2/3/4 -> dropperMachine on the dropper row above the conveyor; Speed 1/2 -> chevrons along the conveyor; ore tiers -> orePile beside the collector; Cash x1.5/x2 -> vault next to the collector; any purchase -> plotWall around the plot edge), each popping in with GameAssets.popIn plus GameAssets.burst. PlotGrowth.clear(player) shrinks and removes them on rebirth. Bump counter plot_growth_built per model. Hook: UpgradeService calls PlotGrowth.apply after every successful purchase and on plot claim; RebirthService calls PlotGrowth.clear after a rebirth reset.

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback must fire within about 3-5s, never 20s. A spec or acceptance text that says 20s is wrong for playtests, so shorten it and keep the tested window consistent. Claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim,
